problem: Existing socially aware ObjectNav methods map human-robot-object (HRO) interactions into one shared feature space, which loses feature specificity because humans, robots and objects interact in different ways.
motivation: Robots in crowded domestic scenes must reach a target object category while respecting human social awareness and using object co-occurrence relations. Humans, robots and objects have different interaction paradigms, so they should be represented separately rather than homogeneously.
key_idea: Learn a Heterogeneous Scene Representation of HRO ternary interactions with a Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network that models each interaction type separately, then use it in a DRL policy for socially aware ObjectNav.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The claim is that keeping interaction types separate preserves feature specificity and improves navigation in crowded scenes over homogeneous modeling.
method: Heterogeneous Scene Representation (HSR): represents HRO ternary interaction features with separate node and edge types for humans, robots and objects.
Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network (HGAN): models the different interactions and semantic relations with type-specific attention so each keeps its essential properties.
DRL-based socially aware ObjectNav strategy: learns HSR-based scene state transition and state value estimation to guide navigation.

setting.backbone: HGAN (heterogeneous graph attention) with a DRL policy, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: not stated in the abstract; presumably simulated crowded domestic scenes

results: The abstract claims the method outperforms existing solutions in challenging domestic crowded scenes, supported by baseline tests and ablation studies. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details on the simulator, data, metrics and real-robot testing are unknown.
